haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes from creation. If not claimed in time, the Inventory expiry sweep (every minute) releases it and returns stock to sale. Order is not told.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved or charged, the customer is told which items are short, and the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses the order id as its idempotency key, so retries with the same key cannot double-charge, per the document.
haiku-low.q4: Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer, and requests a full refund from the snapshot amount. Payment refunds it, and the customer is emailed when refund is issued.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied only when OrderConfirmed arrives, after confirmation. If checkout fails, the cart stays exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: Order moves the checkout through its statuses. The record of how far it has got is the order's status in Order's database.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies it and writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to its outbox for Order. A lost-webhook sweep also asks the provider.
haiku-low.q8: Payment's inbox stores each provider event id with a unique key, so a repeat is dropped and answered 200 OK. Handlers also check current status before acting.
haiku-low.q9: Payment declined triggers Order to set PAYMENT_DECLINED and send ReleaseStock. Inventory releases the hold; if it already lapsed, the release does nothing.
haiku-low.q10: ClaimStock checks the reservation is still HELD and unexpired, in one transaction. If the claim succeeds the order is confirmed; if it fails the order is cancelled and fully refunded.
haiku-low.q11: The refund record goes to RETRYING and is retried with growing delays. A sweeper re-picks it. After N failures it becomes REFUND_FAILED, alerts operations, and keeps retrying. Tracked in Payment's refund records.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event causes Cart to empty the cart. It is the only thing that empties it, and the outbox redelivers until it succeeds.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes (expiry). If not claimed, the Inventory expiry sweep (every minute) turns the HELD reservation into RELEASED and the stock goes back on sale; Order is not told.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge; payment is only requested after the hold succeeds. If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all lines reserved in one transaction or none), Inventory sends StockShort with the short items, order becomes REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, nothing charged, cart unchanged, customer told which items are short.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key: the order id is sent with the charge request (also as the charge reference), and retries reuse the same key, so a retry cannot double-charge.
sonnet.q4: The claim fails (StockClaimFailed), so Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, emails the customer, and sends RefundRequested for the full amount from the snapshot; Payment refunds in full. The order is never shipped in part.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when the order is confirmed (OrderConfirmed event, handled by Cart). On any failure or other order ending, the cart stays exactly as it was.
sonnet.q6: Events on the shared message broker (sent via outbox/relay) move it between services; Order service handles the transitions and holds the status. The record of progress is the order's status in Order's database (with Inventory's reservation status and Payment's payment record per order id holding their own parts).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment; Payment verifies it, updates the payment record and writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to its outbox, which is published as an event on the broker to Order. For success, Order sends ClaimStock to Inventory, and Inventory's StockClaimed/StockClaimFailed event goes back to Order, which finishes the order.
sonnet.q8: Payment's inbox stores the provider event id with a unique key; a duplicate event id means nothing is done and 200 OK is returned. Consumers also keep an inbox of handled event ids (saved in the same transaction as the state change) and check current status, ignoring events that no longer fit. Payment status moves only one way.
sonnet.q9: The reservation is released (stock back on sale). Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED on PaymentDeclined and sends ReleaseStock; Inventory releases the hold (does nothing if the hold already lapsed).
sonnet.q10: Order sends ClaimStock and Inventory checks in one transaction whether the reservation is still HELD and not past expiry. If yes, CLAIMED and the order is confirmed; if not (late success), StockClaimFailed leads to cancellation and full refund. A payment taking over 10 minutes therefore always ends in a refund, even if stock is still free; stock is not re-reserved.
sonnet.q11: The refund record goes to RETRYING and is retried with growing delays; a sweeper re-picks any unfinished refund. After N failed attempts it becomes REFUND_FAILED, the operations team is alerted, and it stays open and keeps being retried after the cause is fixed. It is tracked in Payment's database as a refund record with retry state. (N and delays are open questions.)
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, sent by Order when it sets CONFIRMED, triggers the Cart service to empty the cart. It is the only thing that empties it; the outbox redelivers until it works, and doing it twice is harmless.
